heroHeadline: Fires Keep Fading, But the Bill Arrives: BC's Wildfire Overrun Adds $614M to Provincial Deficit
heroSubtitle: With the acute fire season already winding down — Northwestern Ontario's active count holding near season lows at 31-32 fires after a single tiny new start (Nipigon 112, 0.1 ha) on September 19 — the season's financial toll came into sharper focus this week. British Columbia's first-quarter fiscal update on September 14 showed wildfire-fighting costs running $614 million over budget, a major contributor to a $450 million jump in the province's projected 2026/27 deficit, now near $13.8 billion. On the ground, the Rinker Lake Complex in Northwestern Ontario remains formally not under control but with low activity, and BC's Bald Range, Pear Lake and Ainslie Creek fires remain 'under control' or 'being held'. No new deaths or evacuation orders were identified this cycle.
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
